stop.description: [release] stop the section now when no claim is left (what other sections need stays up)

variants.description: [test] only these env variants of the suites that declare :suite/variants, a,b (default every variant); each selected suite with variants must declare every named one, else refused; a suite without variants runs once. The variant env reaches the suite RUNNER only, never the stack's consumers (no restart or re-env per variant)

agent.description: [claim|release] the agent claiming; defaults to the caller's agent_id

skip_fails.description: [test] a skipped case fails its cell (the case stays skipped in the report); default each suite's :suite/skip-fails?, else false

project.description: [touch] with no target: only the sections of this project; [nrepl] only this project's routes; [flaky] only runs against this project

recreate.description: [restart] recreate the containers (up --force-recreate --no-deps) instead of restarting them in place

path.description: [nrepl] a file or directory: answers the shared nREPL that drives it

run.description: [stack-up|stack-down|stack-status|plan|faults|why|test] the stack run id, ^[a-z0-9]{3,40}$ (stack-up default <stack><6 hex>, test default test<6 hex>); claim/release a run with target=stack:<run>

note.description: [claim] what the agent works on (required with ttl_minutes)

wait.description: [up|switch|stack-up|test] wait until the started services are healthy (stack-up and test: default true)

keep_up.description: [test] keep the stack up even when every cell passed (a failed matrix always stays up)

dry_run.description: [test] answer the matrix, the stack plan and every runner spec; start nothing

env.description: [up|switch|restart] extra environment for compose interpolation, e.g. {"HOST_GATEWAY_IP": "192.168.1.5"}; a value {"pass": "<store path>"} is read from pass when the containers are created, and shown only as pass:<path>. The section remembers it for later up/restart/reaper passes (status call-env-keys); a null value ("VAR": null) forgets VAR (a no-op when not remembered); a reload that changes VAR's declared value forgets it too

no_deps.description: [up|switch] start only the named services, not their depends_on (which must already run)

target.description: [up|switch|down|stop|restart|touch|ps|logs] services or native profiles: name, project/name, or a,b

ttl_minutes.description: [claim] make it a WAVE claim: live for this many minutes (at most :compose/claim-max-ttl-minutes, default 480) whether or not the owner (an agent or a coordinator, agent=coordinator:..) stays in the swarm; claim again to move its end, release to end it now

all.description: [test] run the whole matrix (every suite against every project its suites apply to) when neither suites nor projects is given; without it such a call is refused, naming what it would run (dry_run plans it anyway)

projects.description: [test] projects under test, A,B (default every project a selected suite applies to)

allow_shared.description: [up|switch|restart] recreate a service another live section holds (refused by default, naming the holder section and its agents)

allow_orphans.description: [up|switch|restart] go ahead although processes a dead docker daemon left running still hold the section's volumes or ports (refused by default, naming them)

test.description: [why] the failed test: a case id (orders.place_boom_order) or <suite>/<project>/<case>

description: docker compose sections for local development. Name a TARGET (a service or native compose profile of a configured compose project, e.g. target=sisf-web, target=sisf/frontend, target=sisf-web,sisf-crm) and exactly that runs, closed over the YAML's depends_on; the section's id is <project>/<targets>. Presets from compose-profiles.edn work via profile=ID. A section also starts the host PROGRAMS its project pairs with its services (a shadow-cljs watch, a JVM): a Clojure directory starts with its nREPL, and up/status answer the port. A section keeps alive everything its services depend on, so releasing or reaping another section never stops a dependency this one needs; down/stop name what they kept and why. restart recycles the named services in place (recreate=true recreates them) even when another section needs them, but never recreates (restart recreate=true, or up with other compose files, dir or env) a service another live section holds unless allow_shared=true; the refusal names that section and the agents owning it. up/switch take no_deps (start only the named services, e.g. past a failing migration), wait (until healthy) and env. touch with no target resets every active section. SWARM: an agent working on an app claims its section (claim target=<section, preset or services> note=..; renew within the claim TTL, release when done; claiming an active section never restarts it) and gets the shared nREPL per module to drive instead of starting its own JVM; nrepl path=<file> answers which port drives that file. The reaper keeps a section while it is claimed, agents work in its project or new nREPL connections reach it, and stops it when nobody does: after its TTL, or the shorter orphan TTL once its last claim ended. A WAVE claim (claim ttl_minutes=.. note=.., up to 8 h, owner may be a coordinator) holds until it ends or is released, even when its owner parks or leaves the swarm. STACKS: stack-up stack=<id> runs a stack of capability consumers (shared deps once, opt-outs private, each consumer on its own view network, health-gated); stack-down, stack-status, plan; claim target=stack:<run>. SUITES: test suites=X,Y projects=A,B runs the suite x project matrix on one union stack and answers per-cell verdicts from exit code and JUnit/TAP; a failed matrix stays up for inspection. test with neither suites nor projects is refused unless all=true. STRICT PARAMS: a param a command does not take refuses the call before anything runs (invalid-param naming unknown, valid and did-you-mean, e.g. suite -> suites); the host's own keys (agent_id, directory, async, _meta, _caller_*) are always accepted. command=help lists every command with its params.

command-help.status: active sections: services, idle time, reaper countdown, host programs
command-help.targets: what each configured project offers as a target: services and native profiles
command-help.programs: host programs each project declares, how each starts, whether its nREPL answers
command-help.up: start a section alongside the others; refused while processes of a dead docker daemon hold its volumes or ports. target|profile; no_deps (only the named services), wait (until healthy), env {VAR value | VAR {"pass": path}}, allow_orphans (go ahead anyway); refused when another live section holds a service it would recreate (other compose files, dir or env), naming the section and its agents, unless allow_shared
command-help.switch: make a section current, stopping what only the previous one needed. same params as up
command-help.down: remove a section's containers (never volumes), keeping what other sections need; :kept names those and :note says when nothing was removed. target|profile
command-help.stop: stop a section's containers, keeping what other sections need; :kept names those and :note says when nothing was stopped. target|profile
command-help.restart: restart a section's services in place even when other sections need them; recreate=true recreates the containers (never their depends_on), refused when another live section holds one of them unless allow_shared. A target runs from the section holding its services (its dir, files and env); a recreate's env is remembered by that WHOLE section, so its other services that read a var get it at their next up. target|profile; env; allow_orphans; allow_shared
command-help.touch: reset the idle clock. target|profile for one section; none for every active one; project to narrow
command-help.ps: what a section needs and which of it runs. target|profile
command-help.logs: last log lines of a section. target|profile; tail
command-help.claim: an agent declares it works on a section; on an active or fully running section it only renews or takes it (never starts or recreates a container), else it brings it up through the same guards as up (refused, naming the holder section and its agents, when that would recreate a service another live section holds); the answer names the shared nREPL per module to drive. target (an active section id, a preset id, or services) | profile | target=stack:<run>; agent (default agent_id); note; ttl_minutes (a wave claim, held whether or not the owner stays in the swarm; needs note). Renew before claim TTL
command-help.release: an agent gives up its claim (a wave claim too; agent= names whose claim, and any caller may name any agent: there is no auth); with no claim left the section is reaped after the orphan TTL, or now with stop=true. target (an active section id, a preset id, or services) | profile | target=stack:<run>; agent; stop
command-help.who: per active section: claims (owner, note, wave?, expires-in-seconds), what the last pass saw using it (claims, agents working in its project, new nREPL connections), when it is reaped; per live agent the sections it works in
command-help.nrepl: which shared nREPL drives a module: path (a file or dir) for the closest one, project to filter, none for all; each with advice
command-help.reap: run the idle reaper now (usage pass, then reap)
command-help.adopt: take charge of running containers no section owns
command-help.projects: every compose project on the host
command-help.flaky: test cases ranked by intermittent failure across recorded suite runs, each :flaky, :regression (failing since a named run and sha), :fixed or :stable. suite; project; limit (default 20)
command-help.faults: fault injection on a stack run whose needs go :via :toxiproxy: op add|remove|reset|list (default list); run (run id); proxy (<consumer>.<capability>, see TOXIPROXY_PROXIES); toxic {type latency|timeout|bandwidth|reset_peer|slow_close|limit_data|slicer, attributes {name number}, stream upstream|downstream, toxicity 0..1, name}
command-help.stack-up: run a stack (:compose/stacks): resolve capabilities, start shared and private instances in order, each waited and health-gated, join them to each consumer's view network hive-<run>-<consumer>, then start the consumers with their wiring env. stack; run (default <stack><6 hex>); wait (default true)
command-help.stack-down: take a stack run down: consumers, view networks, then the instances no other live run or section keeps (never volumes, never what ran before the run). run, or stack for every run of it
command-help.stack-status: stack runs with their instances' and consumers' containers now. stack; run
command-help.plan: what stack-up would start, share or find running (terraform-plan style). stack; run
command-help.why: explain a failed test: its case, the deepest error span carrying a message (trace store, :compose/tempo-url), the span path from the root, container logs of its run in its time window and the stack plan; written to <state>/runs/<run>/why/<case>.md+.edn. test (case id or suite/project/case); run (default the newest run holding it)
command-help.test: run the suite x project matrix (:compose/suites): one stack for the union of what the cells need (or the live run named by run), each suite's runner (a container on the projects' view networks, or a host command) with HIVE_RUN_ID, TRACEPARENT and BAGGAGE test.id, JUnit/TAP read from its reports dir; a summary is written to <state>/runs/<run>/summary.edn; down when every cell passed or when no cell ran at all (an error before the first cell), kept up for inspection when one failed (the reaper TTL still applies); a reused run is never taken down. The answer starts with plan {projects, suites, cells, services (containers the stack starts)}. suites=X,Y and/or projects=A,B; with neither (and no run=<live run>) the call is refused, naming what it would run, unless all=true (every suite against every project); run (default test<6 hex>); keep_up (keep a passing stack up); dry_run (plan and runner specs only, nothing starts); wait (default true); variants=a,b (the :suite/variants to run, each a cell <suite>@<variant>, default all; every selected suite that declares variants must declare each named one, else the call is refused; a suite without variants runs once). The variant env is set on the suite RUNNER only: the stack and its consumers are NOT restarted or re-env'd per variant, so a variant that toggles a service's own flag tests nothing (follow-up 20261123122851-6e29b6f7); skip_fails (a skipped case fails its cell). exit 0 every cell passed, 1 a test failed, 2 something could not run. A cell passes only when its runner exited 0 and its report parsed: an unparsable report is could-not-run; a container suite, or one that declares :suite/reports-dir or :suite/report-format, must leave a report with at least one case unless :suite/report-required? false. Every case is listed with id, status and time; a could-not-run cell carries :reason and, when known, :service
